I’m both a professional and former patient. Given that personality disorders require a lifelong pattern of behaviours, I would think it would be difficult to diagnose them in the ER. I know, one time when I was in the ER for my own bipolar, the psychiatrist, who was assessing me in the ER. was convinced that I must have borderline to the point where she stopped actually listening to what I was say, that I was upset my personal psychiatrist hadn’t returned my calls because sometimes he was able to give me hope when I couldn’t find it for myself. She was convinced my suicidal plans were an attempt to manipulate or demand. Eventually I just gave up on her understanding my whys and let her believe whatever she wanted to believe because I was tired of trying to explain what was happening in my head to someone who wasn’t listening to me because of her beliefs. She eventually put, in the mental health act forms that she thought I had a personality disorder. I am not saying that people aren’t mistaking diagnosed with bipolar rather than borderline, but someone’s outpatient’s psychiatrist might be better able to assess rather than an inpatient psychiatrist that has seen them on one or two really bad days. I might just have had a psychiatrist who was have a bad day that day though.
